lessons.goal: 推論物品安排反映的經驗與人物決策。

questions.evidence: Poppy remembers their last trip, when she carried a torn paper bag because nothing more would fit. She removes one book she has already read and a pair of shoes nearly identical to another pair. A small empty space appears beside her clothes.
questions.explanation: 上次箱子放不下，她另提破紙袋。
options: Poppy needed a paper bag because her suitcase was full.
She forgot every pair of shoes.
Her father lost a handmade bowl.
She brought no books.
questions.prompt: What problem occurred on the previous trip?

questions.evidence: Poppy remembers their last trip, when she carried a torn paper bag because nothing more would fit. She removes one book she has already read and a pair of shoes nearly identical to another pair. A small empty space appears beside her clothes.
questions.explanation: 她移除已讀書及重複性高的一雙鞋。
options: The handmade bowl before buying it.
Every pair of shoes.

questions.prompt: Which item does she remove this time?

questions.evidence: Before a family trip, Poppy fills every corner of her suitcase. She packs three books, extra shoes, and several things she says she might possibly need. Her father asks where she will put the small gifts she plans to bring home.
questions.explanation: 問題提醒旅行後段可能新增物品。
options: To test the titles of her books.
To forbid buying anything.
To suggest filling every gap immediately.
To make Poppy consider later storage needs.
questions.prompt: Why does the father ask about gifts?

questions.evidence: During the trip, she uses that space for a handmade bowl wrapped carefully in soft fabric. The empty space was not a forgotten item or wasted effort; it was part of her plan. Poppy does not decide to pack almost nothing next time. She learns that preparation includes considering what may happen later, and that leaving room can be a deliberate choice rather than a failure to fill a container.
questions.explanation: 留白是事先考量後的有意選擇。
options: Forgotten accidentally.
Required by every traveler.
Chosen thoughtfully on purpose.
Done without considering a reason.

It proves her suitcase was originally too large.

questions.prompt: How does the bowl support Poppy's revised plan?

lessons.story:
Before a family trip, Poppy fills every corner of her suitcase. She packs three books, extra shoes, and several things she says she might possibly need. Her father asks where she will put the small gifts she plans to bring home.

Poppy remembers their last trip, when she carried a torn paper bag because nothing more would fit. She removes one book she has already read and a pair of shoes nearly identical to another pair. A small empty space appears beside her clothes.

During the trip, she uses that space for a handmade bowl wrapped carefully in soft fabric. The empty space was not a forgotten item or wasted effort; it was part of her plan. Poppy does not decide to pack almost nothing next time. She learns that preparation includes considering what may happen later, and that leaving room can be a deliberate choice rather than a failure to fill a container.
lessons.title: The Space Left Empty in the Suitcase
